content: 1. The metabolism of tramadol is influenced by cobicistat, which inhibits the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This interaction can lead to increased levels or effects of tramadol. A reduced dose of tramadol may be required, and therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction may also occur through an unspecified mechanism. Cobicistat similarly increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies if necessary. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. The coadministration of triazolam or midazolam (oral) with cobicistat or atazanavir is contraindicated due to significant increases in benzodiazepine concentrations. These drugs are extensively metabolized by CYP3A4, and their levels can rise dramatically, leading to potential toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir has a similar effect. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 6. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Tucatinib also increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Ublituximab decreases the effects of atazanavir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 11. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid or use alternative drugs if necessary. 13. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 14. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely, limiting the dose to 5 mg every 24–72 hours. 15. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase of venetoclax. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 18. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination may increase the risk of atrioventricular (AV) block. 20. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid or use alternative drugs if necessary. 21. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with increased systemic exposure. Consider temporarily withholding antiretroviral therapy if significant side effects develop. 23. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects. Consider temporarily withholding antiretroviral therapy if significant side effects develop. 24. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as the significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Atazanavir and cobicistat increase the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of warfarin by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 and other enzymes. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 32. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zafirlukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 34. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 35. Atazanavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zileuton by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is potential for increased toxicity. 37. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 38. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Cobicistat and atazanavir increase the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
